experiments.question: Which projection of a team's points is most accurate out of sample?
experiments.hypothesis: Schedule-adjusted ratings (D) beat raw averages (A/B); a development-fitted stack (F) adds a little.
experiments.method: A season avg shrunk; B EWMA + raw opponent-allowed; C plays x points/play (raw); D ridge off/def ratings (pf_core.rolling_ridge_ratings, FCS pooled, prior seasons decayed 0.2/yr, alpha per target tuned on 2018-19); D_C ridge plays x ridge points/play; E LightGBM on PIT ratings + context (refit each season); F NNLS stack fitted on 2017-2019 (weights D_C_ridge_opp_x_eff 0.09, D_ridge_sos 0.68, E_lgbm 0.22); G game-level ridge (CFB-TP-02). Validation 2021-22 selected G_game_ridge; holdout scored for the frozen winner.
experiments.data: FBS-vs-FBS regular season team-games; holdout n=3004 (1502 games)
experiments.result: Holdout MAE 8.99 vs A 10.50, retired engine 9.97, script-engine baseline 9.42, closing market 8.84. CRPS diff vs A -0.913 [-1.033, -0.783], vs retired engine -0.625 [-0.729, -0.523], vs market +0.103 [+0.050, +0.158].
experiments.interpretation: G_game_ridge is the most accurate non-market team-points projection on validation and holdout; it remains 0.14 points of MAE behind the closing line.

experiments.question: Can a game-level model of margin and total beat the team-level stack and the archived 2026 'v2' research models?
experiments.hypothesis: Using the full matchup (both teams' offence AND defence ratings across points, EPA, success, pace, yards, plus talent/returning-production differences) beats summing two independent team projections.
experiments.method: Ridge (standardised features) on margin and on total, refit each season on all earlier seasons; alpha chosen on development ({'margin': 100.0, 'total': 3000.0}); team points = (total +/- margin)/2, so coherence is exact. HONESTY NOTE: G was added after the first scoring pass, which had shown on VALIDATION (and on holdout) that the archived v2 research predictions beat the stack on margin/total. Selection still used validation only, but the holdout has now been looked at twice for this family. A data bug found on the live 2026 sample (no 2026 recruiting class -> a missing-data indicator shifted every 2026 margin by +7) was fixed by explicit imputation before final scoring.
experiments.result: Validation team-points MAE G 9.17 vs F 9.29; margin MAE G 12.92 vs v2 12.75; total G 12.64 vs v2 12.71. Holdout margin CRPS vs v2 -0.010 [-0.100, +0.081], total vs v2 -0.041 [-0.098, +0.020], total vs market +0.071 [-0.021, +0.170].
experiments.interpretation: G matches the archived v2 research models on margin and is slightly better on totals, while being reproducible walk-forward inside this package (v2 exists only as archived predictions). Totals are statistically indistinguishable from the closing total on both holdouts; margin remains ~0.35 points of MAE behind the closing spread.

experiments.question: Does adjusting for strength of schedule beat raw opponent-allowed averages?
experiments.hypothesis: Yes: raw points-allowed credits defences that met weak offences.
experiments.method: Paired absolute error, D (joint ridge off/def ratings) vs B (team EWMA + opponent's raw allowed EWMA).
experiments.data: FBS-vs-FBS team-games; development n=5844, validation n=2932
experiments.interpretation: Schedule adjustment is better on validation.

experiments.question: Should FCS opponents be pooled into one rated entity?
experiments.hypothesis: Yes: an individual FCS team has 1-3 games vs FBS, so ridge shrinks it to the league (FBS) average and its opponents' offence/defence absorb the gap.
experiments.method: Paired MAE (game-clustered bootstrap), same ridge settings, only the tested choice changes.
experiments.interpretation: On validation FBS-vs-FBS the pooled/carried version is no detectable difference; in FCS games it is better.

experiments.question: Does carrying prior seasons (decayed) help?
experiments.hypothesis: Yes early in the season; small later.
experiments.method: Paired MAE (game-clustered bootstrap), same ridge settings, only the tested choice changes.
experiments.interpretation: On validation FBS-vs-FBS the pooled/carried version is better; in FCS games it is no detectable difference.

experiments.question: Does a talent/returning-production preseason prior beat simply carrying last season's ratings?
experiments.hypothesis: Regressing last season's rating by returning production and talent improves weeks 1-4.
experiments.method: Current-season-only ridge shrunk toward a preseason expectation (offset). Prior = ridge regression of each team's single-season end rating on last season's carried rating, talent z, returning-PPA z and their interaction, fitted on seasons before the target season only. Compared with the carry model D (diff = prior - D, MAE).
experiments.interpretation: Talent/returning-production prior (Dp_talent_returning_prior_a2.5): week 1 development +0.010 [-0.348, +0.384]; validation wk1-1 -0.089 [-0.544, +0.391] (no detectable difference); wk2-4 +0.131 [-0.100, +0.405] (no detectable difference); wk5-20 +0.033 [-0.030, +0.094] (no detectable difference). No detectable week-1 gain; the carry-only variants (current-season ridge shrunk to last season's carried rating) are identical to D in week 1 by construction and slightly worse in weeks 2-4 than D's joint multi-season fit. Offence-only returning production + talent do not add information beyond last season's schedule-adjusted ratings at this sample size.

experiments.question: Do efficiency ratings built without garbage-time plays forecast better?
experiments.hypothesis: Filtering garbage time removes noise from blowouts and improves forecasts of future EPA and points.
experiments.method: Ridge EPA/play ratings from CFBD all-play vs no-garbage EPA; each mapped to the target by a development linear fit; paired absolute error on the next games' full-game EPA/play and points.
experiments.result: development target epa: no-garbage 0.1297 vs all 0.1291 (+0.001 [+0.000, +0.001]); development target pts: no-garbage 9.9080 vs all 9.9162 (-0.008 [-0.047, +0.032]); validation target epa: no-garbage 0.1348 vs all 0.1344 (+0.000 [-0.000, +0.001]); validation target pts: no-garbage 9.7626 vs all 9.8469 (-0.084 [-0.138, -0.025])
experiments.interpretation: development/epa: filtered is worse; development/pts: filtered is no detectable difference; validation/epa: filtered is no detectable difference; validation/pts: filtered is better.

experiments.question: Is team_points better projected as opportunity x efficiency than directly?
experiments.hypothesis: Decomposing into volume (plays/attempts) and per-play efficiency isolates pace from quality.
experiments.method: Validation CRPS/MAE of C (raw volume x raw rate), D_C (ridge volume x ridge rate) vs D (direct ridge).
experiments.interpretation: The decomposition is roughly equivalent to the direct rating; it earns a small weight in the stack rather than replacing it.

experiments.question: How much should team ratings be pooled, and how fast should last season fade?
experiments.hypothesis: Moderate ridge (5 games) and 0.5/season decay.
experiments.method: Development-only grid (2015-2019 MAE, FBS-vs-FBS): alpha x prior-season decay; plus within-season recency (halflife in days).
experiments.result: alpha 0.75 decay 0.2: 9.634; alpha 0.75 decay 0.35: 9.662; alpha 1.5 decay 0.2: 9.665; alpha 1.5 decay 0.35: 9.680; alpha 2.5 decay 0.35: 9.726; alpha 2.5 decay 0.2: 9.731; alpha 2.5 decay 0.5: 9.799; alpha 5 decay 0.35: 9.866. Within-season recency at alpha .75/decay .2: none 9.6335, 90-day halflife 10.1028, 45-day 10.2534.
experiments.interpretation: Light pooling is best (alpha 0.75, decay 0.2): last season's games at 20% weight already act as the prior, so little extra shrinkage is needed. Recency weighting hurts (it also down-weights the prior season).

experiments.question: How should total and margin distributions be built from team projections?
experiments.hypothesis: Empirical residual pairs (keeping football's lumpy scores and the within-game correlation) beat a bivariate normal and an independent model.
experiments.method: Same team means; development CRPS of total and margin from 3 joint constructions.
experiments.result: empirical: rho 0.047, CRPS total 9.559, margin 9.143; bivariate_normal: rho 0.047, CRPS total 9.575, margin 9.150; independent: rho 0.047, CRPS total 9.574, margin 9.152
experiments.interpretation: Chosen: empirical. All are coherent by construction (one joint sample set).

experiments.question: Discretised normal vs empirical residual vs negative binomial for team-level outcomes?
experiments.hypothesis: Empirical residuals win for points (key numbers), NB for counts.
experiments.method: Development CRPS (in-sample shape choice) on the D model's residuals.
experiments.result: team_points: normal 6.7650, empirical 6.7471, nb 6.8429; plays: normal 5.4888, empirical 5.4705, nb 5.4676; team_passing_yards: normal 48.0798, empirical 47.9067; team_rushing_yards: normal 43.8099, empirical 43.6021; points_per_play: normal 0.0981, empirical 0.0977; epa_per_play: normal 0.0922, empirical 0.0919; success_rate: normal 0.0426, empirical 0.0426
experiments.interpretation: Differences are small (<1% CRPS); empirical residuals are chosen for most families.

experiments.question: Why do the published defensive rankings look unrealistic, and what fixes them?
experiments.hypothesis: Season-to-date-only ratings ranked before the schedule graph connects, with no prior.
experiments.method: Replay of the production adjust.fit_metric (points_per_game) week by week 2016-2025; Spearman rank correlation of each week-w defensive rating with a rating fitted ONLY on weeks >= w (independent data).
experiments.result: Rank correlation with rest-of-season defensive truth (mean 2016-2025): week 2 script engine 0.36 vs ridge-with-carry 0.62 vs raw 0.31; week 4 0.49 vs 0.57; week 8 0.53 vs 0.52. Top-10 overlap with the true top 10 at week 2: 2.0 (script engine) vs 4.4 (carry).
experiments.interpretation: The defensive ranking problem is first a sample/prior problem: in weeks 2-4 the season-to-date method is little better than raw points allowed (rank correlation ~0.36-0.49 with the rest of the season) while the carried rating is already ~0.6. Two secondary distortions are verified: defences that played an FCS team are flattered (next-game points allowed under-projected by 1.3 points in the script engine vs 0.2 with FCS pooling), and per-game points mix in the team's own pace (rank gap vs per-drive correlates +0.34 with own plays). From ~week 6 every method converges to ~0.52: even a good rating identifies only ~4 of the true top-10 defences, so any published rank needs an uncertainty band.

experiments.question: Are the script engine's published CONTROL margin ranges / win rates calibrated on 2026 games?
experiments.hypothesis: Historical tier ranges cover ~50%/80% of 2026 margins.
experiments.method: Frozen 2026 artifacts (data/scripting/live/frozen_v2) joined to final scores.
experiments.data: 25 completed 2026 games carrying a CONTROL claim
experiments.result: central-50 coverage 0.520, central-80 0.760; stated win rate 0.799 vs realised 0.760. Same games, PF joint model: 80% range coverage 0.800, winner Brier 0.177.
experiments.interpretation: Ranges are tier-level historical frequencies, not game-specific forecasts; they should not be presented as probabilities. Sample is small.

error_investigations.impact: Rank correlation with rest-of-season defensive truth (mean 2016-2025): week 2 script engine 0.36 vs ridge-with-carry 0.62 vs raw 0.31; week 4 0.49 vs 0.57; week 8 0.53 vs 0.52. Top-10 overlap with the true top 10 at week 2: 2.0 (script engine) vs 4.4 (carry).
error_investigations.cause: The model behind them is a SEASON-TO-DATE ridge with lambda = 4 games and NO prior-season information, on points PER GAME, ranked across FBS and published even when the fit is flagged unstable (the FBS schedule graph has ~85 disconnected components after week 1 and ~40 after week 2). Shrinkage toward the mean does not change an ordering when every team has the same number of games, so early ranks are the order of 1-3 raw results against unconnected opponents.
error_investigations.action: Rank defences with the carried, schedule-adjusted rating (prior seasons decayed, FCS pooled) and suppress ranks while the schedule graph is disconnected (weeks 1-3); show per-drive or per-play rather than per-game points allowed. Production files were NOT modified (research-only); the replacement is research/projection_foundation/cfb ratings + the team_points family.

opponent_adjustment.summary: Schedule adjustment (joint ridge offence/defence ratings refit before every week) is the single largest gain over raw averages; pooling FCS opponents into one entity is required; carrying the prior season at 20% weight replaces the need for heavy shrinkage.

opportunity.summary: Plays are projectable (holdout MAE ~7.1 plays vs ~7.4 for the season average) but the plays x points-per-play decomposition does not beat the direct schedule-adjusted points rating; it carries a small stack weight. Receiving opportunity is limited to completions (no targets in any CFB box score).

calibration.summary: Distributions are fitted on development residuals only and then frozen. Against OUTCOMES they are calibrated: 80% ranges cover 0.79-0.83 and PIT variance ratios are 0.93-1.03 on validation, holdout, 2025 and 2026. Against the CLOSING LINE they are not useful: the model's P(cover)/P(over) at the closing number has Brier 0.25-0.27 (a constant 50% scores 0.25) and the reliability tables are flat - when the model says 60-70% against the spread the side wins ~49% (holdout). Model-vs-market disagreement is noise, not edge.

failed_experiments.name: Within-season recency weighting of ratings (halflife 45/90 days)
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: Development MAE 9.6335 -> 10.1028 / 10.2534: recency also discounts the prior season, which is the most valuable information early on.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Do not apply calendar decay on top of the season decay; if recency is retried, decay within season only.

failed_experiments.name: Opportunity x efficiency as the primary team-points model
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: Plays x points-per-play (raw or ridge) is no better than the direct ridge rating.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Keep it as a stack component and as the explanation layer for pace, not as the main model.

failed_experiments.name: Raw opponent-allowed adjustment (B)
failed_experiments.what_was_learned: Clearly worse than schedule-adjusted ratings, and it is exactly what makes raw defensive rankings misleading.
failed_experiments.changes_future_decisions: Never rank or adjust by raw points/yards allowed.

defensive_rankings.headline: Rank correlation with rest-of-season defensive truth (mean 2016-2025): week 2 script engine 0.36 vs ridge-with-carry 0.62 vs raw 0.31; week 4 0.49 vs 0.57; week 8 0.53 vs 0.52. Top-10 overlap with the true top 10 at week 2: 2.0 (script engine) vs 4.4 (carry).

Shrinkage toward the mean does not change an ordering when every team has the same number of games, so early ranks are the order of 1-3 raw results against unconnected opponents.
defensive_rankings.action: Rank defences with the carried, schedule-adjusted rating (prior seasons decayed, FCS pooled) and suppress ranks while the schedule graph is disconnected (weeks 1-3); show per-drive or per-play rather than per-game points allowed. defensive_rankings.interpretation: The defensive ranking problem is first a sample/prior problem: in weeks 2-4 the season-to-date method is little better than raw points allowed (rank correlation ~0.36-0.49 with the rest of the season) while the carried rating is already ~0.6. Two secondary distortions are verified: defences that played an FCS team are flattered (next-game points allowed under-projected by 1.3 points in the script engine vs 0.2 with FCS pooling), and per-game points mix in the team's own pace (rank gap vs per-drive correlates +0.34 with own plays). From ~week 6 every method converges to ~0.52: even a good rating identifies only ~4 of the true top-10 defences, so any published rank needs an uncertainty band.

pf_core_findings.finding: No group/hierarchical offsets: an entity with 1-3 rows is shrunk to the league average. In CFB that rates every FCS opponent like an average FBS team, flattering whoever played them (FCS-game MAE +1.4 to +2.0 points vs pooling).
pf_core_findings.workaround: Relabel all non-FBS teams to one 'FCS' entity before calling.

pf_core_findings.finding: Fits every block present over ALL earlier rows (no history window) with a dense one-hot design; cost grows with history (~0.3-0.5 s per refit here).
pf_core_findings.workaround: Season-blocked relabelling (prior seasons collapsed into one block) and per-season calls; ratings cached on disk.

pf_core_findings.finding: halflife_days decays prior SEASONS too (on top of prior_season_decay); with CFB this costs ~0.5 points of MAE (9.63 -> 10.10).
pf_core_findings.workaround: Not used; documented as a failed experiment.

pf_core_findings.finding: The home-advantage coefficient is ridge-penalised with the team effects (sklearn Ridge penalises every coefficient). Harmless at the small alphas chosen here, biased toward 0 at large alpha.

Thresholds are not sport-aware: |log factor| > 0.35 is 'extreme' and any factor with < 3 opponent games is flagged; in CFB this flagged 44% of all team projections (a top defence legitimately moves expectations 30-50%, and every week-1 opponent has 0 games).
pf_core_findings.workaround: Factor not passed to pf_core; CFB checks (opponent beyond 2.5 SD of FBS; weeks 1-4 opponent sample) in cfb/gate_cfb.py.

pf_core_findings.finding: The 5% mean/pmf tolerance BLOCKs a correct distribution when the published mean is the model mean but the pmf is floored at 0 (low projections).
Returns a frame with a fresh RangeIndex (season merge) and inserts columns one by one (pandas fragmentation warnings, slow per-entity lambdas).
pf_core_findings.workaround: Merge results back on keys, never on index.
